target.title: fix: launchd reload handoff strands gateway when restart races the drain window
target.body:
Closes #110137

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where macOS users restarting the gateway while any run was active (plugin activation, upgrade, or any plist-rewriting restart selecting handoff `mode=reload`) would have the gateway exit after its drain and **never relaunch** — the LaunchAgent left deregistered, port free, `KeepAlive` a no-op — until a manual `launchctl bootstrap` (~29 minutes of downtime in the report).

The reload handoff waits only 15 × 0.2s ≈ 3s after `launchctl bootout` for the label to disappear. But a booted-out gateway keeps the label registered until its drain-before-exit window completes (up to 300s, `DEFAULT_RESTART_DEFERRAL_TIMEOUT_MS`). Whenever the drain outlasts the 3s poll: `launchctl bootstrap` fails with `Bootstrap failed: 5: Input/output error` mid-bootout, the `kickstart -k` fallback cannot succeed on a booted-out label, and the handoff exits leaving the service deregistered — deterministically, per the issue's logs (attempt→failure in exactly 3 seconds against a 300s drain).

## Why This Change Was Made

Two changes to the reload handoff script, matching the issue's expected behavior ("wait out the drain budget, and in every failure case leave the label bootstrapped"):

1. The post-bootout unload poll now covers the full drain budget plus margin: 315 × 1s, with the count derived from `DEFAULT_RESTART_DEFERRAL_TIMEOUT_MS` (now exported from `src/infra/restart.ts`) so the two windows cannot silently drift apart. The poll still exits as soon as the label actually unloads, so restarts with no active runs remain as fast as before.
2. The single dead `kickstart -k` fallback becomes a bootstrap retry loop: bootstrap failures retry (up to 15 × 1s), and `kickstart -k` only fires when `launchctl print` shows the label is actually registered — the one case where kickstart can work. The handoff can no longer exit with the service deregistered, which is the invariant #84630 established for reload handoffs.

## User Impact

Restarting the gateway while agent runs are active now works on macOS launchd installs: the handoff waits for the drain, bootstraps the rewritten plist, and the gateway comes back — instead of staying down until manual intervention. Idle restarts are unchanged (verified: no added latency when the label unloads immediately).

## Evidence

Focused tests (all green):

```
pnpm test src/daemon/launchd-restart-handoff.test.ts
 Tests  5 passed (5)
pnpm tsgo  → exit 0
```

Beyond script-text assertions, both the pre-fix and post-fix generated scripts were **executed for real** against a simulated `launchctl` (a state machine modeling: label stays registered while the old gateway drains, `bootstrap` → EIO while registered, `kickstart` only succeeds on a registered label). Same script bytes production spawns, driven through `/bin/sh`:

```
# incident scenario — restart with an active run (8s simulated drain)
old script: gives up in 4s, exit 113, service stranded        ← the reported outage
new script: waits out the drain (8s), exit 0, service running

# transient bootstrap failure after unload
old script: kickstart fallback dies on booted-out label → unloaded (the ~29min outage state)
new script: bootstrap retry recovers in 3s → running

# idle restart (no active runs)
old and new both: exit 0, service running, 0s — no added latency

Synthia QC panel: 5/5 anchor checks passed, fidelity 100.0
```

**Real macOS LaunchAgent lifecycle proof** (added after review feedback). A throwaway LaunchAgent (`ai.openclaw.test110137`, own plist with the production `ExitTimeOut` pattern, `RunAtLoad`) runs a daemon that traps SIGTERM and drains 20s before exiting — the gateway's drain-before-exit shape. Both generated handoff scripts were executed for real against `gui/501` launchd (real `bootout`, real `launchctl print` polling, real `bootstrap`, real relaunch; paths redacted, no production service involved):

```console
# OLD (pre-fix) script — real launchd, 20s drain
{"case":"old","exit":37,"elapsedSeconds":3,"finalLabelState":"stranded","daemonRestarted":"no"}
daemon.log: started pid=…  → got SIGTERM, draining 20s → drain complete, exiting
# exit 37 in exactly 3s — the issue's literal handoff-log values — and after the
# drain finishes the label is deregistered forever: the reported outage.

# NEW (this branch) script — identical scenario
{"case":"new","exit":0,"elapsedSeconds":20,"finalLabelState":"registered","daemonRestarted":"yes"}
handoff log: restart attempt …Z → restart done exactly 20s later
daemon.log: drain complete, exiting → daemon started (new pid, same second)
```

The earlier simulated-`launchctl` matrix (above) additionally covers the transient-bootstrap-failure and no-drain scenarios; the live run confirms its semantics match real launchd (`Bootstrap failed: 5: Input/output error` was observed live when bootstrapping mid-unload).

**Review follow-up addressed** — the effective drain budget is now threaded through: `restartLaunchAgent` resolves `gateway.reload.deferralTimeoutMs` via `resolveGatewayRestartDeferralTimeoutMs` and passes it to the handoff, so a config-raised deferral timeout scales the bootout wait instead of reopening the race (regression test pins 600s → `bootout_wait_count="615"`, and unbounded `<=0` configs keep the finite default wait). Branch rebased onto current `main`.

---

**AI-assisted:** authored with Claude Code (Claude Fable 5); before/after script execution matrix scored with the Synthia QC panel as described above. I understand what the code does and reviewed the diff by hand.
